instruction.text: Write in the gap to complete the idiom.

wrong.text: to throw someone under the bus – to betray someone or to let someone down
wrong.sound: to throw someone under the bus means to betray someone or to let someone down

atoms.b: Let's ((spill)) the beans about the difficult situation with our teacher!

wrong.text: Spill the beans! – to let out a secret
wrong.sound: Spill the beans means to let out a secret

atoms.b: My friend always wants to ride ((shotgun)). Otherwise, he feels dizzy.

wrong.text: to ride shotgun – to ride in the front passenger seat
wrong.sound: to ride shotgun means to ride in the front passenger seat

atoms.b: Before I write the exam, I need to get my ducks in a ((row)) by creating a structured studying plan.

wrong.text: to get one's ducks in a row – to prepare well for something
wrong.sound: to get one's ducks in a roaw means to prepare well for something

atoms.b: Everybody in our group needs to ((bring)) something to the table.

wrong.text: to bring something to the table – to provide something that's beneficial
wrong.sound: to bring something to the table means to provide something that's beneficial

atoms.b: My grandfather always said he wanted to travel the world before he kicked the ((bucket)).

wrong.sound: to kick the bucket means to die

atoms.b: Learning a new language takes patience and practice. Rome wasn't ((built)) in a day.

wrong.text: Rome wasn't built in a day – important things take time and consistent effort
wrong.sound: Rome wasn't built in a day means that important things take time and consistent effort

atoms.b: I'll try to keep you in the ((loop)) so you know what we'll decide.

wrong.text: to keep someone in the loop – to make sure to inform someone and keep them updated
wrong.sound: to keep someone in the loop means to make sure to inform someone and keep them updated.

atoms.b: While we're waiting to give our presentation, we should just sit ((tight)) and try not to worry too much.

wrong.text: Sit tight! – to wait patiently and not take any action
wrong.sound: sit tight means to wait patiently and not take any action

atoms.b: I'd love to go to school with you tomorrow, but I feel a little sick, so I'll have to take a ((rain)) check.

wrong.text: to take a rain check – to reschedule an invitation
wrong.sound: to take a rain check means to reschedule an invitation

atoms.b: The cancellation of the concert was a ((blessing)) in disguise, as it allowed us to spend more time together at home.

wrong.text: a blessing in disguise – an apparent misfortune surprisingly leads to a positive outcome
wrong.sound: a blessing in disguise means an apparent misfortune surprisingly leads to a positive outcome

atoms.b: When my friend told me about some rumours at school, I knew I should take it with a ((grain)) of salt.

wrong.text: to take something with a grain of salt – to view a statement or situation with scepticism
wrong.sound: to take something with a grain of salt means to view a statement or situation with scepticism

atoms.b: When it comes to the importance of a peaceful learning environment, both teachers and students see eye to ((eye)).

wrong.text: to see eye to eye – to agree with someone
wrong.sound: to see-eye-to-eye, means to agree with someone

atoms.b: I really enjoyed this conversation, because he directly addressed the issue without beating around the ((bush)).

wrong.text: to beat around the bush – to avoid getting to the main point because it feels uncomfortable
wrong.sound: to beat around the bush means to avoid getting to the main point because it feels uncomfortable

atoms.b: When building the new school building, the construction team committed to quality and did not cut ((corners)) to ensure everything is following the guidelines.

wrong.text: to cut corners – doing something quicker often sacrificing quality or ignoring rules
wrong.sound: to cut corners means doing something quicker often sacrificing quality or ignoring rules
